incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Quebec Business Corporations Act (QBCA), CQLR c. S-31.1, ss. 7-16 (incorporation and articles), s. 35 (contents), s. 45 (registered office), s. 79 (board of directors); complemented by the Act respecting the legal publicity of sole proprietorships, partnerships and legal persons, CQLR c. P-45, ss. 11-12 (registry declarations). Alternative federal incorporation: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 5.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), Centre de services aux enterprises, online portal: Registre des entreprises du Québec (REQ).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) filed electronically with the REQ, together with the initial declaration of registered office and directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the QBCA. Shares may be issued with a low par value or no par value; any subscribed-but-unpaid share consideration becomes a receivable of the corporation. A private business corporation has no escrow account requirement; escrow deposit rules apply only to specific immigration-investment or public-listing structures.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscriptions to the common shares of the Corporation be and are hereby accepted, and that such shares be issued fully paid and non-assessable upon receipt of the consideration; RESOLVED THAT the registered office of the Corporation be established at the address set out in the Articles of Incorporation, in Quebec, Canada, and that the officers file all declarations with the Registraire des entreprises; RESOLVED THAT [Name] be appointed President and Chief Executive Officer and [Name] Secretary-Treasurer, each with customary signing authority; RESOLVED THAT the banking mandate of the Corporation be opened with a chartered Canadian bank to support wire transfers and letters of credit, and that all acts consistent herewith be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Conduct Corporate Name Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - NUANS Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) request through the REQ portal to verify the proposed corporate name against existing registrations and trademarks. File a name reservation request if availability must be secured before filing the articles. Alternatively, proceed directly with a numbered company name (e.g., '1234-5678 Québec Inc.') to avoid this step.
required_dossiers: List of proposed names in priority order (up to three)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, submit an amended list of proposed names or switch to a numbered company. A formal review may be requested under the Act respecting legal publicity within 30 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator(s); notary for paper filings; REQ authenticated online system for electronic execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Statuts de constitution (Articles of Incorporation) setting out the corporate name, registered office address, share class structure (common shares with or without par value), transfer restrictions if any, number of directors, and mandatory special provisions. Ensure at least one director is a natural person resident in Canada, as required by the QBCA. Execute the articles digitally or sign before a notary for paper filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution)
Name reservation certificate (if not using a numbered company)
Proposed director list with residential addresses
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar identifies a defect, revise the articles and re-execute; for paper submissions, legalize signatures before a notary or other authorized attesting officer and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Application with the Enterprise Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Articles of Incorporation and the initial declaration containing the registered office address, municipal address, names and residential addresses of directors, and the act constituting the legal person. Pay the statutory incorporation fee of CAD 352 (approximately USD 259) plus applicable registry service fees by secure online payment. Retain the REQ transaction receipt for the corporate record book.
required_dossiers: Initial declaration of directors and registered office
Registered office address and mailing address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The REQ issues a notice of correction describing the defect; cure by filing the amended document within the stated period (usually 15-30 days). If the application is refused, revise the articles and submit a new application; no material prejudice arises beyond delay and the re-filing fee, if any.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Publish Registry Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once validated, the Registraire issues the Certificat de constitution; the corporation legally exists on the certificate date. The REQ automatically publishes the incorporation in the enterprise register, and certified extracts may be downloaded for banking and client-side know-your-customer verification.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is not issued, confirm the refusal reason and either seek review of the registrar's decision or re-file an amended set of articles. Data-entry errors in the certificate are corrected by submitting a request for correction to the REQ.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Bylaws and Execute First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors; REQ for registrable changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting (or obtain unanimous written consent) to adopt By-law No. 1 covering share transfers, meetings, directors, officers, and indemnification; approve the form of share certificates and corporate seal if used; elect officers as set out in the First Board Resolution; open the corporate minute book and issue share certificates to subscribers. File any registrable director changes with the REQ within the statutory delay.
required_dossiers: First Board Resolution (as set out above)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Procedural omissions are cured by a subsequent written resolution signed by all directors or shareholders; late-filed declarations are regularized by filing a corrective declaration with the REQ and, where necessary, obtaining a waiver of late-filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Bank Accounts and Initiate Quebec Tax Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate operating account using the Certificate of Incorporation, First Board Resolution, and officer identification; request wire transfer and letter-of-credit facilities to support the project cargo payment rails. Simultaneously register with Revenu Québec for GST/QST and employer accounts so that the corporation can invoice and remit taxes from commencement. This step overlaps with Stage 3 tax registration but is initiated here to unlock banking.
required_dossiers: Bank account application and AML questionnaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the authorization, issue a revised banking resolution confirming signatories; if Revenu Québec requests additional evidence, provide incorporated certificates and director declarations. Any missing declaration is filed online with the REQ or Revenu Québec portal to cure the defect.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for non-asset-based ISIC 5229 freight arrangement. Contingent authority: Commission des transports du Québec (CTQ) if the corporation later operates its own heavy-haul commercial fleet in Quebec.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None applicable for a project cargo logistics arranger. Contingent license: Transport Operating Certificate (Certificat de transport) under the Act respecting transportation by motor vehicle, CQLR c. T-12, if operating commercial vehicles for own account.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP), Government of Quebec
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no mandatory Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2, for an office-based freight arrangement. A declaration of activity would be triggered only if a fixed industrial establishment or storage facility were later operated.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not triggered for pure logistics services. If future warehousing or maintenance is added: municipal wastewater discharge limits, Quebec Clean Air Regulation (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1) VOC thresholds, and Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG) registration under the federal TDG Regulations for any hazardous project cargo handling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal occupancy permit and local fire safety certificate for the registered office and any transloading yard; CNESST registration and compliance with the Quebec Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c. S-2.1) including emergency evacuation planning; structural load clearances obtained by the landlord for leased premises; no special security clearance required for standard project cargo brokerage.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange administration is exercised jointly by the Department of Finance Canada and the Bank of Canada under Canada's flexible exchange-rate regime, with FINTRAC administering AML/ATF obligations. There is no dedicated FX control agency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains near-total convertibility for both current and capital account items. The Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) establishes the Canadian dollar as legal tender, but contractual settlement in any freely convertible foreign currency is permitted. No exchange-control restrictions impede profit remittance, dividends, loan repayments, or capital repatriation for a Quebec business corporation, subject to solvency tests under the Quebec Business Corporations Act (CQLR c S-31.1) and any applicable non-resident withholding tax on dividends and interest (typically 15-25% reduced under tax treaties). The project cargo entity may freely invoice and receive in CAD, USD, EUR, or other currencies. Inbound equity and outbound trade payments do not require Bank of Canada approval. GST/HST and Revenu Québec registration are separate tax obligations, not FX controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada has not imposed foreign exchange surrender or repatriation requirements for export proceeds since 1951. An out-of-gauge heavy-haul logistics company is not required to repatriate foreign-currency earnings within any statutory timeline, nor convert any percentage into Canadian dollars. Export invoices must be retained for tax, statistical, and customs purposes under the Customs Act and Census and Statistics Act, but there is no central-bank conversion mandate. All settlement may remain in the currency of the underlying contract.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-Medium. Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (SC 2000, c 17) and FINTRAC regulations, any offshore digital EMI carrying on business in Canada must register as a money services business (MSB) in Canada. An unregistered foreign EMI cannot lawfully provide payment services to a Canadian-bound project account. Offshore EMI accounts are not deposit accounts with chartered-bank protections and cannot issue MasterCard/Visa settlement reliably for high-value milestones. They may be used only for ancillary low-value collections if the EMI is FINTRAC-registered and prepared to accept the funding-wire documentation. The primary treasury, capital injection, LC, and clearing needs must be handled through a Schedule I or Schedule II Canadian bank. A treasury policy should therefore designate the EMI as a wallet-type sub-ledger, never as the bank clearing account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal or Quebec banking statute statutorily requires directors to appear physically in branch for account opening. FINTRAC's Client Due Diligence and Ongoing Obligations Regulations (SOR/2016-146) permit remote identification when supported by reliable documentation and a risk-based approach. However, for a newly formed federal or Quebec corporation whose directors are all non-resident, most tier-1 Canadian banks will require at least one officer or director to attend an in-branch interview or a video conference corroborated by a notarised certificate of incumbency issued by a Quebec notary, attorney, or bank correspondent. Remote opening is available where the bank has an existing relationship or where the applicant provides certified true copies of passports plus a NIV (notary identification verification) signed by a Canadian notary public. Physical presence is the de facto standard for first-time non-resident corporations and is recommended to avoid 30-60 day onboarding delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident parent and offshore UBO ownership exceeding 25% of the Canadian project-cargo entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified true copies of federal and Quebec incorporation certificates; current shareholders' register; passport copies of every beneficial owner; corporate organisation chart; FATCA/CRS self-certification forms; and beneficial-ownership schedule with PEP screening results.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound equity injection in excess of CAD 500,000 to procure heavy-haul equipment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the capital contribution; signed subscription and share-purchase agreement; bank statement proving source of wealth of the remitting shareholder; shareholder registry update; transaction purpose code for direct equity investment; three-year cash-flow forecast aligned with ISIC 5229 project-cargo scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account title and activity indicate high-value cross-border supplier wire flows to countries with elevated sanctions risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master logistics service agreement; commercial invoices and pro forma contracts for out-of-gauge cargo movement; supplier onboarding file including business licence, sanctions-screen negative results, and bank counterparty details; FINTRAC-compliant transaction monitoring narrative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No Canadian credit history, no established economic nexus, all directors non-resident
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec head-lease agreement (physical office or bonded terminal); Quebec Transport Ministry permits for over-dimensional cargo; Revenu Québec GST/QST registration or voluntary registration certificate; utility bill or lease proof; one-year project schedule and Canadian customer letter confirming heavy-haul engagement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of commercial Letters of Credit with potential for trade-based money laundering and dual-use equipment red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete LC transaction file (SWIFT MT700/MT707); bills of lading from a recognised ocean or rail carrier; customs broker declaration; electronic bills of lading where applicable; third-party inspection certificate for the out-of-gauge cargo; end-user certificate or project-site delivery confirmation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections should be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV from the shareholder's bank to the Canadian bank's clearing account. The wire instruction must include the beneficiary account number (CIS), the ISO payment-purpose code for direct investment (e.g., 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' or 'Equity Injection'), a narrative stating 'Share capital injection for Quebec project cargo corporation', and full remitter identification. For amounts above CAD 10,000, Canadian banks will verify the source of funds and may request a closing balance confirmation from the remitting bank. The funds will post to the operational account only after FINTRAC sanctions screening and against the corporate subscription ledger. If the injection is structured as shareholder debt, the instruction should include a loan agreement and transfer price documentation to avoid tax recharacterisation. Dividends, management fees, and royalty disbursements are non-controllable, but withholdings under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act must be remitted by the entity at source.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for heavy-haul equipment and project-cargo subcontractor milestones should be executed through the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier and subcontractor payments, including the beneficiary's full account details and the trade-invoice reference; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) for purchase of oversized equipment or milestone-based EPC disbursements; (3) Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) using SWIFT MT400/MT422 for progressive payment terms; (4) CAD settlement in excess of CAD 50,000 is cleared through Canada's Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) operated by Payments Canada using the bank's clearing code and settlement account; (5) USD settlement is cleared via the correspondent bank network, CHIPS, or Fedwire, depending on the downstream bank. Each outbound wire must be referenced to the underlying commercial invoice and the Canadian bank's AML model must match the payee against OSFI/DPR sanctions lists. If controlled goods under the Export and Import Permits Act are involved, additional customs permits must be appended.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable vanilla FX forwards on CAD pairs (USD/CAD, EUR/CAD, GBP/CAD) under ISDA 1998 FX and Currency Definitions
European-style FX options on CAD pairs, including puts and calls on monetised collateral
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) where delivery of the foreign currency is prohibited or illiquid; CAD itself is fully deliverable
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) linking CAD borrowing to USD/EUR project revenue streams
FX swaps and tom-next rollovers for interim liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada – Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation; there is no fixed calendar-year deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for one year after written notice from the Director may trigger administrative dissolution under CBCA section 212; the corporation loses standing until revived or restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Declaration / Annual Update (Déclaration annuelle) under the Quebec legal publicity regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the enterprise's registration in Quebec; confirms directors, registered office, and principal activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent failure for two consecutive years may lead to cancellation or dissolution of the registration by the Registraire and loss of legal personality in Quebec; administrative penalties may also apply under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return included as an annual statutory filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and Revenu Québec for provincial corporate income tax, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the taxation year-end; balance-due remittance is generally due 2 months after year-end, or 3 months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 5% penalty on the unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months, with higher penalties for repeat failures; continued non-compliance may result in prosecution and enforced collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue, asset, or employee-size threshold is prescribed under the CBCA or the Quebec Business Corporations Act for a private business corporation; an independent auditor is mandatory only if the corporation is a distributing or publicly accountable entity, or if the shareholders do not pass the annual resolution waiving the auditor appointment.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial statements must be prepared under IFRS (Part I of the CPA Canada Handbook) for publicly accountable entities, or under Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) for non-distributing private corporations; records must support the statutory accounts and CRA reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual return or annual declaration date, the corporation must confirm the individuals with significant control, namely persons owning or controlling 25% or more of the shares or controlling the corporation in fact; changes to the significant-control register must be recorded within 15 days. The register remains available for lawful regulatory inspection but is not a routine public statutory filing under current CBCA and Quebec rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0–USD 5,500 per year; nil if audit is waived by shareholder resolution, or CAD 3,000–CAD 7,500 if a full statutory audit is engaged

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal and Quebec general corporate income tax rate: 26.5% (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%). A combined 12.2% rate (federal 9% + Quebec 3.2%) applies to a Canadian-controlled private corporation's first C$500,000 of active business income, subject to phase-outs.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Key incentives: federal small business deduction (SBD), Quebec small business deduction, SR&ED expenditure tax credit (federal 15% non-refundable; Quebec refundable up to 30%), accelerated CCA for clean-energy equipment, Atlantic/provincial investment tax credits, and Quebec refundable tax credits for manufacturing and logistics automation.
